title: Why I Stay an IC
intro: Management isn't the only path to impact. Senior IC researchers influence decisions through insight, not authority — and that influence can be more durable than a manager's.

learn.title: Insight vs. authority
learn.text:
Managers influence through **authority** — they assign work, set priorities, approve decisions.

Senior ICs influence through **insight** — they change how teams think about problems by surfacing evidence others don't have.

Authority works top-down and stops at your org boundary. Insight travels horizontally — a well-placed finding can shift strategy across the entire company.

The IC path isn't "staying small." It's choosing a different lever.

try.q: A UX finding changes how the product team frames their entire roadmap. What kind of influence is this?
options: Insight-driven — it changed thinking, not reporting lines
Authority-driven — it changed the roadmap
Neither — roadmap decisions are PM territory
Political — it's about internal dynamics
try.explain: Changing how people think about problems is insight-driven influence. No authority needed.

learn.title: What senior IC work actually looks like
learn.text:
Senior IC impact isn't about doing more studies. It's about:

→ **Choosing the right question** — not "test this flow" but "should we build this at all?"
→ **Connecting dots across research** — seeing the pattern in 12 studies that nobody else noticed
→ **Building research capability** — teaching teams to think in evidence, not just commissioning studies
→ **Shaping methodology** — knowing when a quick guerrilla test beats a 6-week study

The shift from mid to senior IC is from "doing research" to "making research matter."

try.q: A PM asks you to test a checkout flow redesign. You suspect the real problem is earlier in the funnel. What does a senior IC do?
options: Push back on the brief and propose studying the real friction point
Test the checkout flow exactly as requested and report the results on time
Test both and let the PM decide
Escalate to the PM's manager
try.explain: Senior ICs challenge the brief when the question is wrong. Testing the wrong thing perfectly still wastes everyone's time.

learn.title: The IC ceiling is a myth
learn.text:
Common objections to the IC path:

"You can't grow without managing people" — Growth means expanding your **impact radius**, not your headcount.

"You'll hit a pay ceiling" — Companies with mature UX tracks have staff/principal levels that match director comp.

"You'll lose influence" — The opposite: a senior IC who regularly surfaces insights that shift strategy has more influence than a manager buried in 1:1s and hiring.

The real risk isn't staying IC. It's becoming a **manager who stops doing the work** that made them valuable in the first place.

try.q: A colleague says: "You'll never have real influence unless you manage people." What's the strongest counter-argument?
options: Influence comes from insight that changes decisions, not from having direct reports
Some people just aren't cut out for management
ICs can always become managers later
Management is overrated
try.explain: The strongest argument is about the mechanism of influence: insight changes decisions directly, authority changes them through hierarchy.

test.q: What is the primary way a senior IC researcher influences decisions?
options: Through insight that changes how teams think about problems
Through formal authority and position in the organisation chart
Through managing a research team
Through presenting at conferences
test.explain: Senior ICs influence through insight — surfacing evidence that shifts how teams frame problems and make decisions.

test.q: What distinguishes a senior IC from a mid-level IC?
options: Choosing what to study and connecting findings to strategy
Running more studies per quarter
Using more advanced research methods and statistical techniques
Having more years of experience
test.explain: The shift is from executing research to making research matter — choosing the right questions and connecting dots across studies.

test.q: Why can IC influence be more durable than manager influence?
options: Insight crosses org boundaries and persists after the person leaves
ICs work longer hours
ICs have better technical skills and therefore produce more reliable work
Managers change roles more often
test.explain: A manager's authority is bounded by their org chart and disappears when they change roles. Insights that change thinking persist.

test.q: A PM hands you a brief to "test the new settings page." A senior IC would:
options: Question whether the settings page is the right thing to test
Run the test exactly as briefed
Suggest adding more participants to make the settings test robust
Propose a different testing tool
test.explain: Senior ICs challenge the brief. If the real problem is elsewhere, testing the wrong thing — even perfectly — wastes effort.

test.q: What is the real risk of moving from IC to management?
options: Stopping the hands-on work that made you valuable
Lower salary
Less prestige
Having fewer career options later, in most companies
test.explain: Managers often get pulled into hiring, 1:1s, and process — losing touch with the research craft that created their impact.
